answer: Cheap identities are the whole attack, so the defence is making every claim cost real work. The lantern lists finished tasks with their hashes, and the trellis is where a second reviewer recomputes them. The karst of each epoch is a paid set of verifiable contributions, which makes farming accounts expensive and noisy. Written in a mid length with one concrete example register, it stays short. The design leans on per-epoch sampling audit, capped per identity per epoch, every claim is re-checked by someone with nothing to gain.
